_readme: Cloud round lock. ONE cloud chief round works at a time. This file is tracked on purpose - it is the only lock in this project that travels between machines, because it is not guarding a machine's resources but the right to be the round that is running. It is won by PUSHING it, never by writing it: git rejects a non-fast-forward push atomically, and that rejection is the only real mutual exclusion this system has. If your push is rejected, another round won and YOU END YOUR ROUND IMMEDIATELY - no retry, no force, no rebase-and-try-again. Losing is the correct answer.
_procedure: 2. read this file. state HELD and heartbeat_utc newer than stale_after_hours => END THE ROUND NOW. Write one line saying which round holds it. Do not clone the code repo, do not read source, do not spawn subagents, do not plan work.
3. free => write HELD + round + session + utc, commit, push
4. push rejected => another round won => END THE ROUND NOW
5. push accepted => you hold it => start working
6. during a long round, refresh heartbeat_utc and push about every 20 minutes
7. at the end, write RELEASED, commit and push - ALWAYS, including when the round failed
_takeover: A round may take the lock from a holder only when heartbeat_utc is older than stale_after_hours. Record takeover_of with the abandoned round number. Never take it because it 'looks dead' - cloud sessions die silently and that is exactly why the threshold exists.

_field_notes.session: any string that identifies the run; used only to tell two rounds apart
_field_notes.heartbeat_utc: refreshed about every 20 minutes while working

note: Bootstrap value written by chief round 108 on Panya's bridge, so the first cloud round finds a well formed file instead of deciding what to do about a missing one. No cloud round has ever held this lock.
